calibration_passages.text: Database normalization organizes relational tables to reduce avoidable duplication. First normal form requires atomic column values and no repeating groups; higher forms address dependencies between attributes.
Atomicity means a transaction's operations succeed together or are rolled back together. A transfer that debits one account and credits another must not leave only the debit committed.
HTTP status codes describe the outcome of a request. A 2xx code indicates success, 4xx generally indicates a client-side request problem, and 5xx indicates a server-side failure.

The SameSite cookie attribute controls when browsers attach a cookie to cross-site requests. Strict is restrictive, Lax permits some top-level navigations, and None permits cross-site use when Secure is also set.
A Git commit records a snapshot of tracked project content and points to its parent commit. A branch is a movable reference to a commit, while a tag usually names a release point.
A container image is a packaged filesystem and metadata used to create containers. A running container is an instance of that image with its own process and writable layer.

Photosynthesis uses light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into energy-rich organic molecules, releasing oxygen in oxygenic photosynthesis. Chlorophyll absorbs light in the photosynthetic apparatus.

Cellular respiration extracts usable energy from organic molecules. In aerobic respiration, oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain, and ATP is produced through several coupled processes.
In the water cycle, evaporation moves liquid water into the atmosphere as vapor, condensation forms droplets or ice crystals, and precipitation returns water to Earth's surface.
Plate tectonics describes the movement of rigid lithospheric plates over the underlying mantle. Interactions at convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries produce different geological features.
Two events are independent when learning that one occurred does not change the probability of the other. For independent events A and B, the joint probability is P(A and B) = P(A) times P(B).
The median is the middle observation after values are ordered, or the mean of the two middle observations for an even count. It is less sensitive to extreme values than the arithmetic mean.
Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference; it is not a substance stored inside an object. Internal energy describes microscopic energy within a system.

validation_passages.text: The ACID property of atomicity makes a transaction all-or-nothing. If a transaction fails before commit, its partial updates are rolled back rather than left as a visible subset.
Isolation controls how concurrent transactions observe one another's intermediate work. Isolation levels trade concurrency against anomalies such as non-repeatable reads or phantom rows.
A database index stores an access structure that can speed selected lookups, often at the cost of additional storage and slower writes because the index must also be maintained.
An inner join returns rows whose join condition matches in both inputs. A left outer join retains every left-side row and fills right-side columns with null where no match exists.
An ecological niche describes the conditions and resources a species uses and its role in an ecosystem. It is broader than the physical place where the organism is found.
A food web links multiple feeding relationships in a community. It represents alternative energy pathways more realistically than a single linear food chain.
Ecological succession is a change in community composition over time. Primary succession begins where soil is absent, while secondary succession follows disturbance where soil remains.
Pollination transfers pollen from an anther to a receptive stigma. Fertilization is a later event involving the union of reproductive cells, so the terms are not interchangeable.
Albedo is the fraction of incoming solar radiation reflected by a surface. Snow and ice generally have higher albedo than dark ocean water, so surface changes can alter absorbed energy.
Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, affecting Earth's energy balance. The natural greenhouse effect warms the surface; increasing concentrations strengthen this effect.
Weather describes atmospheric conditions over short periods and local areas. Climate summarizes patterns and variability over longer periods, commonly assessed across decades.
Climate mitigation reduces greenhouse-gas emissions or increases their removal. Adaptation reduces harm from climate impacts, such as preparing infrastructure for heat or flooding.
Power is the rate of energy transfer, measured in watts. Energy is an amount accumulated over time, so a device's power rating alone does not state how much energy it uses in a day.
Energy efficiency compares useful output with energy input. Improving efficiency provides the same service with less energy, although total consumption can still rise if usage expands.
Grid-scale batteries can shift electricity across time by charging when supply is available and discharging later. Storage moves energy; it does not create net energy.
An electric grid balances supply and demand while moving electricity through generation, transmission, and distribution systems. Frequency control is one indicator of real-time balance.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Most arteries carry oxygen-rich blood, but the pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.
Veins return blood toward the heart. The pulmonary veins are an exception to the common oxygen pattern: they carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.
Alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs across a thin surface. Oxygen diffuses into nearby capillary blood while carbon dioxide diffuses toward the air space.
A nephron is the kidney's functional filtering unit. It filters blood plasma and modifies the filtrate through reabsorption and secretion to help form urine and regulate body fluids.

holdout_passages.text: Igneous rocks form when molten rock cools and solidifies. Intrusive igneous rocks cool slowly underground and often develop larger crystals than rapidly cooled extrusive rocks.
Sedimentary rocks form from deposited particles, chemical precipitates, or organic material that becomes compacted or cemented. Layering is common but not universal.
Metamorphic rock forms when existing rock changes under heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids without completely melting. Its original minerals or textures may be altered.
A geological fault is a fracture or zone of fractures along which blocks of rock have moved relative to each other. The motion may be vertical, horizontal, or oblique.
Crop rotation changes the crop grown in a field across seasons. Rotations can interrupt some pest cycles and vary nutrient demands, especially when crops with different traits are alternated.
Many legumes host root-nodule bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms. The amount available to a following crop depends on species, management, and soil conditions.
Drip irrigation delivers water through emitters near plant roots. It can reduce evaporation and water applied between rows, but performance depends on maintenance and system design.
Soil texture is determined by the relative proportions of sand, silt, and clay. Texture influences water retention and drainage, while soil structure describes how particles aggregate.
Torque measures the turning effect of a force about an axis. Its magnitude depends on force and the perpendicular lever arm, and its SI unit is the newton metre.
Linear momentum is mass multiplied by velocity and has direction. In an isolated system, total momentum is conserved when external forces have zero net impulse.
Friction is a contact force that opposes relative motion or its tendency between surfaces. Its magnitude depends on surface conditions and normal force in simple friction models.
Buoyant force acts upward on an object immersed in a fluid. Archimedes' principle states that its magnitude equals the weight of the displaced fluid.
A sample is a subset of a population selected for observation. How the sample is selected affects whether its results can be generalized to the population.
A confounder is associated with both an exposure and an outcome and can distort their apparent relationship. Adjustment may help, but only when assumptions and measurements are adequate.

A confidence interval is produced by a procedure that, under its assumptions, covers the fixed parameter at a stated long-run frequency. It is not generally a probability statement about the parameter after data are observed.

A p-value is the probability, under a specified null model, of observing data at least as incompatible with that model as the observed data. It is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth passes between the Sun and Moon and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. It can occur only near a full moon when the bodies align sufficiently closely.
Moon phases arise from the changing fraction of the Moon's sunlit half visible from Earth as the Moon orbits. The phases are not caused by Earth's shadow except during a lunar eclipse.

Astronomical redshift describes spectral features shifted toward longer wavelengths. For distant galaxies, cosmological redshift is associated with expansion of the universe, with interpretation depending on the cosmological model.
A light-year is a unit of distance: the distance light travels in vacuum during one year. It is not a unit of time, despite the word year in its name.
